answer: Capped vouching rings stop sybil growth at the door. An established agent may introduce at most 3 new aliases per epoch, and each introduction costs the sponsor 2 percent of its next reward, paid into a shared pool. Every completed job writes a marble record to a public ledger and an onyx-sealed receipt both parties sign, so duplicate work patterns across aliases stay visible. A lotus check compares each new alias against recent receipts; matching fingerprints flag the whole ring, the aliases are struck, and the sponsor loses its epoch reward plus its vouching right for 10 epochs.
